mood.summary: Fear is still running high. On Nov 5 the S&P 500 fell 4.4% and the Nasdaq slid into a correction, the worst day since April 2025, on worries that election results will slow AI and data-centre spending. The Fear & Greed index sits in Extreme Fear at 20, and bearish individual investors outnumber bulls by about 14 points. Stocks are bouncing on Nov 6 after a strong jobs report (165,000 jobs vs about 60,000 expected), but that also firmed bets on a December Fed rate hike.

items.name: NVIDIA Corp
items.about: Nvidia designs the graphics processors and AI accelerator chips used in most large data centers.
items.why: Nvidia reported its fiscal third quarter after Tuesday's close, its first report since Jensen Huang resigned as CEO amid a board and Justice Department inquiry; consensus was about $109B in revenue and $2.47 EPS. Shares closed down 0.4% at $155.48, roughly 35% below the Oct 6 record, after dipping to $150.35 intraday. Posts say the numbers beat, but the after-hours reaction was still unsettled when the board was taken.

items.name: SELLAS Life Sciences Group Inc
items.about: SELLAS is a clinical-stage biotech developing cancer immunotherapies, led by the vaccine galinpepimut-S.
items.why: SELLAS said its pivotal Phase 3 REGAL trial of galinpepimut-S in acute myeloid leukemia met its overall-survival goal, with median survival of 24.0 vs 14.7 months (hazard ratio 0.59); full data and a confidence interval have not been released. The stock jumped about 157% to $19.17 from $7.47 on 110M shares after touching $24.86. Posts say a proposed share offering followed after the close, and shares slipped to about $18 after hours.

items.name: Nike Inc
items.about: Nike designs and sells athletic footwear, apparel and equipment worldwide.
items.why: Nike held its Investor Day on Nov 16-17. Posts say it set long-range goals out to fiscal 2031 but warned fiscal 2028 would still be a hard year. The stock opened higher, touched $40.67 and then reversed to close down 6.3% at $35.86 on about 56M shares, roughly double normal volume.

items.name: fuboTV Inc
items.about: fuboTV runs a sports-focused live TV streaming service in North America.
items.why: Shares swung as high as $8.49 before closing at the day's low of $6.88, down 6.9%. No company news was found for the day. Posts focus on the stock sitting at record lows after its 1-for-12 reverse split earlier in 2026.

items.name: Unitedhealth Group Inc
items.about: UnitedHealth is the largest US health insurer and also owns the Optum health-services business.
items.why: The stock fell 5.4% to $389.75, sliding steadily from a $401.47 open. Posts say a newly proposed CMS rule would tighten Medicare Advantage audits and pressure insurer margins, which could not be confirmed by this run. Options traders still bought about $20.5M of calls, according to a flow tracker cited in the stream.

items.name: Snap Inc
items.about: Snap owns Snapchat, a camera-first messaging and social media app funded by advertising.
items.why: Snap rose 8.0% to $5.50, near the day's high, on about 67M shares while the broad market fell. No company news was found; posts speculate about a partnership announcement but cite no source.

items.name: Intellia Therapeutics Inc
items.about: Intellia develops CRISPR-based gene-editing therapies for genetic diseases.
items.why: Shares slipped 0.8% to $9.78 after an early move above $10. No company news was found; posts center on short sellers and patience until data expected in early 2027, and the stream picked up alongside SELLAS's biotech rally.

items.name: GraniteShares 2x Long NVDA Daily ETF
items.about: NVDL is an ETF that aims to deliver twice Nvidia's daily return.
items.why: Traders used the 2x Nvidia fund to position for Nvidia's results after the close, pushing volume to about 43M shares. It closed down 0.7% at $16.24 after falling as low as $15.14 when Nvidia dipped intraday.

items.name: Target Corp
items.about: Target runs about 2,000 US general-merchandise stores and an online shop.
items.why: Target reports its fiscal third quarter before the open Wed Nov 18. Posts say options imply a move of about 7-8% and note that the full-year EPS guide includes roughly $1.65 of one-time tariff refunds. The stock eased 0.5% to $159.52 after a strong run this year.

items.name: Costco Wholesale Corp
items.about: Costco runs membership warehouse clubs selling groceries and general merchandise in bulk.
items.why: Posts say Stifel started coverage at Buy with a $1,220 target, while others point to a forward P/E near 49x, close to its five-year high. Shares dipped 0.3% to $1,110.49.

items.name: Walt Disney Co
items.about: Disney owns theme parks, cruise lines, film studios, ESPN, ABC and the Disney+ streaming service.
items.why: Disney reported fiscal fourth-quarter results; posts say EPS of $1.77 and revenue of about $25.9B beat forecasts, alongside a 33% dividend increase and about $3B of cost cuts. The stock jumped to $122.70 early but faded to close down 1.5% at $116.96 as the market sold off; posts say Wells Fargo kept an Overweight rating with a $132 target.

items.name: SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust
items.about: SPY is the largest ETF tracking the S&P 500 index of large US companies.
items.why: The S&P 500 fund fell 1.0% to $732.42 for a second losing day as software stocks sold off ahead of Anthropic's expected IPO and traders waited for Nvidia's results. October retail sales rose 0.2%, slightly above forecasts. Posts note the fund closed right at its 200-day moving average, near $730.

items.name: Intuit Inc
items.about: Intuit makes TurboTax, QuickBooks, Credit Karma and Mailchimp.
items.why: Intuit fell 7.2% to $320.65, among the worst large-cap losers, as software stocks slid on worries about competition from AI developers ahead of Anthropic's listing; Salesforce and ServiceNow also dropped sharply. Posts say Intuit reports its fiscal first quarter later this week, against a guide of $2.44-2.48 non-GAAP EPS.

items.name: VanEck Semiconductor ETF
items.about: SMH is an ETF holding about 25 of the largest chip designers and makers, with Nvidia its biggest weight.
items.why: The chip ETF swung from $466 to $445 and back, closing down 0.4% at $460.17 as traders positioned for Nvidia's results. A Stocktwits News item said California's attorney general flagged 'red flags' in a state review of the Nvidia-Huang matter.

items.name: First Solar Inc
items.about: First Solar is the largest US maker of thin-film solar panels.
items.why: Shares fell 5.8% to $152.96 alongside a sharp drop in Canadian Solar. No company-specific news was found; posts note the stock is about 52% below its 52-week high and argue about US solar policy.

items.name: Direxion Daily Technology Bull 3X Shares

items.why: The 3x tech fund dropped as low as $116 during the software selloff before recovering to close down 2.8% at $124.24. The stream is mostly active traders posting intraday buys and sells ahead of Nvidia's results.

items.name: Canadian Solar Inc
items.about: Canadian Solar makes solar modules and develops solar and battery storage projects worldwide.
items.why: Canadian Solar dropped 14.8% to $7.81, closing near the day's low. No company news was found and posts describe the slide as unexplained; it trades well below its 50-day average near $11.

items.name: Klarna Group plc
items.about: Klarna is a Swedish payments and buy-now-pay-later company that also offers a debit card and banking services.
items.why: Klarna rose 4.8% to $14.28 on about 15M shares after reporting third-quarter results on Nov 17, following an 8.6% gain on Nov 14 when it named a new CFO. Posts say US volume grew 24% and card volume more than doubled, while others call the Q4 revenue outlook weak.

items.name: Upstart Holdings Inc
items.about: Upstart runs an AI-based lending marketplace that matches borrowers with banks and credit unions.
items.why: Shares fell 5.0% to $18.15, near the day's low, as consumer-lending fintechs weakened. No company news was found; posts point to large put buying and talk of a new 52-week low.

items.name: Omeros Corp
items.about: Omeros is a biopharma company whose lead drug narsoplimab treats a transplant-related blood disorder.
items.why: Omeros fell 16.6% to $13.91 after dropping as low as $12.71. No news was found for the day; posts compare the drop to earlier regulatory setbacks, and long-time holders discuss the company's buybacks and convertible-note retirement.
